Both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass cleanly.

## Summary

The bug was in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts`: `destroy()` fetched the post and deleted it without ever calling `this.authorize()`, unlike `update()` which calls `authorize('update', [Post, post])`. The `PostPolicy` already defined a `delete` ability (author-only check) that was simply never invoked. I added `await this.authorize('delete', [Post, post])` before the delete call, matching the existing `update` pattern exactly — so a non-author now gets a 403 (via `AuthorizationException`) and the post survives, while the author's delete flow is unchanged, and guests are still blocked upstream by the `auth` route-group middleware (redirect to `/login`) or by CSRF, same as the existing `update` route.

I also added feature tests in `tests/PostController.test.ts` (new `describe('posts.destroy', ...)` block) covering: the author successfully deleting their post, a signed-in non-author getting a 403 with the post left intact, and a guest being redirected to `/login` with the post left intact — using `TestApp.fromApp`, `actingAs`/`withCsrf`, and `resetDatabase()` against the real test SQLite DB.
